summary.prose: This Story moves the two controller review tools onto the review pipeline, so a review run from the controller side walks the same calls the daemon would make. Every new controller review is handed emit_calls frames: the review's pending calls, each with its own identifier, packed up to the chunk limit. The controller answers each one, by identifier, in a new answers phase, or reports that it could not complete it (too large, stalled, transient error). Under the limit a review gets today's prompts in one frame and gives today's result. A divided review is handed its chunks about one at a time, and a state saved before this change still finishes on today's frames.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: A new shared module, the review pipeline (proposed at src/workflow/review-pipeline), owns the three stages for every review. It is a serialisable job: the daemon drives it to the end; the controller is handed its calls one frame at a time and answers them by call identifier. Prepare measures material at 3 characters per token against review.chunkTokens (default 128,000 tokens); at or under the limit it emits one chunk whose prompt is the adapter's current single-call prompt, otherwise it groups the adapter's atoms by the adapter's relations and packs whole groups into chunks that each fit, adding a short summary of each related atom held in another chunk. Review issues one call per chunk serially; every call carries a fresh UUID that the answer must echo inside an envelope, an answer whose identifier is missing or wrong is rejected and retried under a new UUID, and a size refusal re-divides the chunk instead of resending it. Gather passes a single chunk's answer through unchanged and otherwise applies the adapter's gather rules (keyed obligations judged on all chunks' evidence, cross-chunk relationships, cross-chunk duplicates), each gather call itself bounded by the chunk limit. ISSUE-aef82b03's delivered InputTooLargeError, LLMProvider.inputBudgetChars, packIntoBatches and ReviewJob loop are moved under the pipeline as its core. A review kind is a series of stages, each a model stage or a deterministic one, preserving today's execution exactly: code review runs one stage per dimension exactly as today on each path: on the daemon, adherence (no call at all when there is neither an approved LLD nor an approved plan), conventions, coverage, quality and functional coverage are model calls, ux is deterministic and provider-free, and diagram keeps its registered handlers (some deterministic, such as the component handler) with today's per-handler isolation, a failing handler still recorded as a LOW observation; on the controller path the ux and diagram prompts are offered to the controller as today; HLD/LLD template review is one reviewer-session stage; DEF/plan premise review is extract (model), probe (deterministic) and verify, where the daemon path verifies one premise per call and the controller path verifies every premise in one batched call, as each does today; an adapter therefore declares its stage plan per path (daemon or controller). A review under the limit therefore makes exactly today's calls in today's order. Each call names its execution mode: a structured call run in the repository as its working directory (as today's code-review judges pass subject.repoPath; for the premise review's verify calls, which pass no working directory today, this is an additive change), each with its own per-call time limit where it has one today (the premise verify call keeps its 3-minute VERIFY_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS from ISSUE-d4b2cd1c), or a read-only reviewer session with the repository as working directory, the review's remaining deadline and its cancellation signal. Ollama gains a reviewer session through a generic read-only tool loop extracted from the analyzer's runShaperToolLoop, taking caller-supplied messages, answer schema, deadline, signal and retry policy, while the analyzer keeps its own wrapper unchanged. The pipeline owns every retry of a review call: every provider is called with internalRetry: false (CliProvider's transient retry and reviewer-session retry, and both providers' structured-output retry, make exactly one attempt), and the pipeline re-issues a transient failure, a stall, an invalid answer or an identifier mismatch once, under a new UUID: two attempts in all per call. Failure policy is per stage: a cancelled review always ends at once; a premise-review verify call that fails both attempts records that premise as not judged (MED, never a pass) and keeps the rest, as ISSUE-d4b2cd1c delivered; a diagram handler failure stays a LOW observation, as today; any other failed call (premise extraction included) fails the review and records nothing, as today. Gather is bounded at every step: an obligation's evidence (notes from every chunk, each keyed by the obligation and carrying the atom ids it stands for) is packed into the final adjudication call when it fits the limit; when it does not, it is reduced level by level, each reduction call reading one batch of that key's evidence and returning one note of at most a quarter of the limit under the same key, the job keeping which atoms and earlier notes each note stands for, until the key's evidence fits one adjudication call; a gather call refused for its size is re-planned like a chunk. Scope of the identifier and limit rules (stakeholder decision 2026-10-19 [[c14]]): they apply to every request the pipeline sends. A reviewer session's internal tool turns belong to the session, as they already do inside the claude and codex CLIs, where insrc cannot see them; the Ollama session's tool loop is likewise not identified or measured per turn. Every call records which material it carries (its chunk, atom ids and evidence-note ids), and the job keeps an immutable snapshot of the review's material taken once at prepare: for code review, today's grounding snapshot (the controller step already saves subject and grounding) plus every fact a deterministic stage reads from disk today, recorded at prepare (the ux stage's companion-mock existence checks); for design review, the document text and, for the premise review, the extracted claims and their gathered evidence. The adapter is rebuilt on every turn from the saved subject plus that snapshot and never re-queries the code graph or the files, so a refused call is re-divided from exactly the material it carried and a controller review resumes on the same material. A controller reports a call it could not complete as a failure outcome keyed by the call's identifier (size refusal with the reported limit, stall, transient error), which the driver handles exactly as a daemon-side failure: a size refusal re-divides the call, the others are re-issued once under a new identifier.

ownedContracts.name: Controller call frames
ownedContracts.purpose: The one frame shape both controller steps use for every new controller review, one chunk or many: the review's calls, each with its identifier, and the controller's answers matched by call identifier. Only a controller state saved before the change resumes on today's emit_judgements / judgements (code review), emit_claims / claims and emit_verdicts / verdicts (DEF/plan premise review) and emit_findings / findings (HLD/LLD template review) frames.

consumedContracts.name: ReviewMaterial
consumedContracts.purpose: What an adapter hands the pipeline to prepare: whole indivisible atoms, the relations between them, and the obligations a gather must judge.

consumedContracts.name: ReviewAdapter
consumedContracts.purpose: How a review kind plugs into the pipeline: its material, its ordered stages (model or deterministic) with each stage's own failure policy, each stage's calls for the whole review and for one chunk, and the gather rules for a divided review.

consumedContracts.name: ReviewChunk and ChunkPlan
consumedContracts.purpose: The output of prepare: the chunks a review is read in, each within the limit, with summaries of related atoms held elsewhere.

consumedContracts.name: CallEnvelope
consumedContracts.purpose: Every model call of every review carries a fresh identifier the answer must echo, and every retry is the pipeline's own re-issue under a new identifier; one rule for daemon and controller. The rule covers every request the pipeline sends; a reviewer session's internal tool turns are the session's own.

consumedContracts.name: ReviewPipelineJob
consumedContracts.purpose: The serialisable state of one review's pipeline run, driven to the end by the daemon or one frame at a time by the controller.

consumedContracts.name: Chunk limit setting
consumedContracts.purpose: One limit for every provider and every review kind.

boundary.internal: The two controller steps' use of the job, and the MCP boundary that admits it: the new answers phase in the insrc_review_step and insrc_code_review_step input schemas in src/mcp/server.ts, their registered schema contracts and tool descriptions, with schema and surface tests (src/mcp/__tests__/schema-registry.test.ts); keeping it in step state, frame sizing, answer validation by call identifier, and offering a review under the limit today's prompts as identified calls in the same frame shape. Compatibility: the controller step states gain an optional pipeline field; a state without it (saved before the change) is resumed on today's path; both stores are memory-only, so, as today, a state does not survive a daemon restart. Tests: S005/ac1 a controller review over the limit is handed the daemon's chunks one frame at a time and records the same kind of result; ac2 a missing or wrong identifier in an answer is rejected and the call offered again under a new UUID; ac3 a new controller review under the limit is offered today's prompts, each as an identified call, and gives today's result; a pre-change state resumes on today's emit_judgements / judgements (code review), emit_claims / claims and emit_verdicts / verdicts (DEF/plan premise review) and emit_findings / findings (HLD/LLD template review) frames, each path tested. The answers phase also accepts a failure outcome per call (size refusal with the reported limit, stall, transient error), mapped to the driver's failure handling and admitted by both MCP input schemas; tested: a controller-reported size refusal re-divides the call, a reported stall or transient error re-issues it once under a new identifier.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The pipeline module itself: measurement, the generic grouping that packs related atoms together within the limit, staged execution with deterministic stages, the envelope schema wrapping, identifier generation and checking, the pipeline-owned retry policy (providers called with internalRetry: false; one re-issue under a new UUID, two attempts in all), per-stage failure policies, refusal re-division, the serial daemon driver, single-chunk pass-through, the bounded gather machinery (evidence notes keyed by obligation, level-by-level reduction under a note cap, provenance kept in the job, refused gather calls re-planned), and the adoption of ISSUE-aef82b03's InputTooLargeError, inputBudgetChars, packIntoBatches and ReviewJob loop. Change sites beyond the new module: CliProvider (internalRetry honoured by withTransientRetry, runReviewSession and its structured-output retry; a size refusal in the claude reviewer-session error envelope and the codex session classified as InputTooLargeError, as completeStructured already does), OllamaProvider (internalRetry: false maps completeStructured to one attempt; a read-only reviewer session over a generic tool loop extracted from runShaperToolLoop in src/analyze/context/driver.ts, the analyzer keeping its own wrapper), and the single-chunk adapters for both review kinds, so every review takes the pipeline path from s1 on with today's calls and working directory (structured calls run in the repository, as today for code review; the premise review's verify calls gain it as an additive change): one model stage per model-judged code-review dimension, adherence making no call without an approved LLD or plan, ux deterministic on the daemon and diagram's handlers as today (deterministic ones stay deterministic, a failing handler stays a LOW observation); one reviewer session for HLD/LLD; extract, probe, then one verify per premise for DEF/plan, with ISSUE-d4b2cd1c's not-judged recording kept. Tests: S001/ac1 an under-limit code review, template review and premise review each make today's calls and give today's result (recorded fixtures), the diagram dimension included; ac2 a missing or wrong identifier is retried once under a new UUID and no prompt hash repeats, including transient errors, stalls and invalid answers on both CliProvider and OllamaProvider; premise extraction failing fails the review while a verify call failing twice records the premise as not judged; ac3 the default limit is 384,000 characters for every provider; ac4 a size refusal from completeStructured, the claude session envelope and the codex session re-divides the call and never resends it; ac5 a review on an Ollama provider completes through both execution modes; plus a live probe of the envelope schema on claude and codex. Also tested: an obligation whose evidence exceeds the limit is reduced level by level, every gather call fits, and the final verdict keeps every atom's provenance; every structured review call runs in the repository working directory. Also tested: a premise verify call keeps its 3-minute limit through the pipeline; a refused call is re-divided from exactly the atoms and notes it carried; the controller premise review under the limit still sends one batched verify prompt. Also tested: refusal re-planning reads only the job's material snapshot, never the graph or files, so a reindex between turns cannot change the material a call is re-divided from. The ux stage reads companion-mock existence from the snapshot's file facts recorded at prepare, not from disk; tested: adding or removing a mock after prepare does not change the review result.

The code-review adapter's material: changed-symbol atoms, call relations from the grounding's callers and callees among changed symbols, file and module relations, and how neighbour summaries are written for a changed symbol held in another chunk. Tests: S002/ac1 related changed symbols land in the same chunk before file and module grouping; ac2 a call relation cut between chunks yields a neighbour summary on both sides; ac3 every changed symbol appears whole in some chunk and one over the limit is named, never cut.

The code-review adapter's gather: per-dimension chunk prompts, obligation keys and their adjudication over all chunks' evidence, the cross-chunk relationship check, the cross-chunk duplicate comparison for quality, and the fold into today's DimensionResult and verdict. It also owns the acceptance smoke: Epic c2ba6fa6 Story s1's code review runs on the installed daemon, completes and records a verdict, with the chunk plan and calls per stage written to the smoke record. Tests: S003/ac1 a divided review and the same material reviewed in one call under a raised limit give the same obligation verdicts on fixtures that fit both ways; ac2 a mismatch between related functions in different chunks is reported; ac3 a cross-chunk duplicate is reported; ac4 the installed-daemon smoke above.

The design-review adapter: document sections as atoms, cross-reference relations, section summaries for neighbours, chunk prompts for the template checklist and the premise pipeline, and the gather of checklist answers or premise verdicts into today's ReviewReport and verdict rules. Tests: S004/ac1 every section appears whole in some chunk with the sections it references; ac2 a cross-chunk reference yields a section summary; ac3 a divided HLD/LLD review and a divided DEF/plan review each give one ReviewReport under today's verdict rules, and a premise whose call fails twice is still recorded as not judged. Its controller stage plan keeps today's single batched verify prompt under the limit; over the limit it batches premises per chunk.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase C — the controller walks the same chunks

nonFunctional.performance: Calls are serial (k6). A review under the limit makes the same number of calls as today. Every prompt sent, chunk or gather, is at most review.chunkTokens x 3 characters.
nonFunctional.security: No new transport: calls go through the existing LLMProvider and the installed CLIs (k7). Reviewer sessions keep their read-only tool sets.
nonFunctional.observability: Each review logs its plan (single or N chunks, chars per chunk), every call's identifier, stage and size, every identifier mismatch and refusal, and the gather's obligation count; DimensionResult and ReviewReport record the number of calls per stage when a review was divided.
nonFunctional.durability: The job is serialisable, so the controller path survives across turns in the existing step state (memory-only, so not across a daemon restart, as today). A daemon review whose call fails after its retries records nothing, as today, except the premise review, which records that premise as not judged and keeps the rest (ISSUE-d4b2cd1c). New record fields (pipelineCalls) are optional, under a new name, and absent on one-chunk reviews; the existing parts field keeps its shape; so existing records keep validating.

api.name: EmitCallsFrame (sc7)
api.signature: interface EmitCallsFrame { readonly next: 'emit_calls'; readonly guidance: string; readonly calls: readonly ReviewCall[]; readonly progress: { readonly stage: string; readonly answered: number; readonly pending: number }; readonly state: string }

parameters.name: calls
parameters.purpose: Every currently pending call of the review's jobs that fits, in a fixed order (code review: today's dimension order; design review: stage order). Packed so that the summed rendered size of the calls (messages, envelope schema and execution) is at most limitChars; a call is never split. Each carries a fresh callId and the envelope schema { callId (const), answer }.

parameters.name: progress
parameters.type: { stage: string; answered: number; pending: number }
parameters.purpose: Where the review stands, for the controller and the log.

returns.meaning: Returned by phase='start' for every new controller review, and by phase='answers' while calls remain. Under the limit, a code review's calls are today's emit_judgements prompts, one call each. They share ONE frame when their summed rendered size fits limitChars, as today's frame does for ordinary reviews; if several single-chunk dimension calls each fit but not together, they are spread over as many frames as needed, never split; a premise review's frames hold the extract call, then the single batched verify call; a template review's frame holds the one findings call.

preconditions: The step state holds the review's jobs in its pipeline field.
postconditions: Only the stages that each adapter's stagesFor('controller') marks 'deterministic' are run daemon-side with runStage before a frame is built: the premise review's probe and the deterministic diagram handlers. The code review's ux and diagram prompts are offered to the controller as calls, as today's emit_judgements frame offers them (src/daemon/steps/code-review-step/handler.ts:439).

api.name: AnswersInput / CallFailure (sc7) and the 'answers' phase handler
api.signature: interface AnswersInput { readonly phase: 'answers'; readonly answers: readonly (EnvelopedAnswer | CallFailure)[]; readonly state: string }; interface CallFailure { readonly callId?: string | undefined; readonly failure: { readonly cause: 'size-refusal' | 'stall' | 'transient'; readonly maxChars?: number | undefined; readonly detail?: string | undefined } }; handleAnswers(input: AnswersInput): Promise<EmitCallsFrame | <tool>Done | <tool>Error>

parameters.name: answers
parameters.purpose: One entry per call of the last frame: { callId, answer } or { callId, failure }.

parameters.name: state
parameters.purpose: The token the last frame returned.

returns.meaning: Each EnvelopedAnswer goes to applyAnswer and each CallFailure to applyFailure (size-refusal with maxChars re-divides the call; stall or transient re-issues it once under a new callId). Entries are classified inside handleAnswers (the MCP schema admits any entry). A malformed entry, an entry with no callId or a non-string one, an unknown callId, or a repeated one is matched to no call: it is ignored and logged. Every call of the last frame without exactly one valid entry is applied as identifier-mismatch, so it is re-issued once under a new callId. A missing identifier therefore reaches the same recovery as a wrong one (S005/ac2). Then the next frame is returned, or, when every job is done, the tool's record is written exactly as today (code review: the CR record through today's runner path, with coverage normalised once; design review: the report stamped as today) and today's done frame is returned.

errors.condition: answers is missing or not an array. Individual malformed entries are not an error; they leave their call unanswered, which is re-issued.

The token is unknown, as today for code review. For insrc_review_step this is a deliberate change: today its dispatch turns StateTokenNotFound into 'internal' (src/daemon/steps/review-step/handler.ts). It now catches StateTokenNotFound and returns 'state-not-found' like code review.
A call in a fail-review stage failed both attempts; nothing is recorded, as today.

preconditions: The state's pipeline field is present.
postconditions: No answer is applied to a call it does not name.

api.name: handleStart (insrc_code_review_step and insrc_review_step)

returns.meaning: Unchanged routing (daemon reviewer vs controller reviewer, confirm_wait, errors). When the controller is the reviewer, it now builds the review's jobs (createReviewJob with path 'controller' for each code-review dimension, or one design-review job), saves them in the state's pipeline field with the subject and snapshot, and returns the first EmitCallsFrame instead of emit_judgements, emit_claims or emit_findings. Every place that today creates a controller review state switches to the pipeline. For code review that is BOTH the fresh-grounding branch AND beginDiffOnlyReview (src/daemon/steps/code-review-step/handler.ts:382), reached from a decline (:263), a freshness timeout (:313) and hollow grounding (:353). The diff-only state keeps its diff-scoped subject, groundingMode 'degraded', fallbackReason, and the warn cap applied when the record is written (capVerdictAtWarn).

errors.condition: As today; AtomTooLargeError from prepare is returned as an error naming the item.

postconditions: New controller reviews always use emit_calls.

api.name: CodeReviewStepStatePayload / ReviewStepStatePayload
api.signature: readonly pipeline?: { readonly jobs: readonly ReviewPipelineJob[]; readonly limitChars: number; readonly lastFrameCallIds: readonly string[] } | undefined

parameters.name: pipeline
parameters.purpose: Present for every review started after this change. Absent: the state was saved before it, and resumes on today's phases.

returns.meaning: Kept in the existing memory-only stores, unchanged: at most 100 entries, with idle entries older than one hour swept opportunistically when a state is saved, so a token idle longer than an hour can still load if no save has swept it. A state does not survive a daemon restart, as today.
Kept only for states without a pipeline field (saved before the change). Called with a pipeline state, they return bad-phase naming 'answers'.

errors.condition: A legacy phase used on a pipeline state.

api.name: MCP input schemas and registry (src/mcp/server.ts)
api.signature: insrc_review_step phase: z.enum(['start','claims','verdicts','findings','answers']) + answers?: z.array(z.unknown()); insrc_code_review_step phase: z.enum(['start','judgements','answers']) + answers?: z.array(z.unknown())

returns.meaning: The tool registry's phase lists gain 'answers' (src/mcp/server.ts:81, src/mcp/server.ts:87), and both tool descriptions describe the emit_calls / answers loop and the failure outcomes, so insrc_schema returns them.

postconditions: The MCP boundary admits any array entries. The installed SDK rejects the whole call when its zod schema fails (validateToolInput), so entry shapes are NOT checked there. handleAnswers classifies each entry instead: a well-formed answer ({ callId: string, answer }), a well-formed failure ({ callId: string, failure: { cause in size-refusal | stall | transient, maxChars?: positive integer, detail?: string } }), or malformed (anything else, including no or a non-string callId and an unknown cause). A malformed entry is ignored and logged, and its call is re-issued as identifier-mismatch, so one bad entry never rejects the turn.
The tool description documents both entry shapes, so insrc_schema shows them even though the schema is permissive.

api.name: Review and code-review guide sections (src/prompts/steering-block.md)
api.signature: the 'review' and 'code-review' sections served by insrc_guide (guideGetResult) and stamped into marked repos' CLAUDE.md by the boot steering refresh

parameters.name: section text
parameters.purpose: The step-by-step loop each guide gives a controller.

returns.meaning: Rewritten so a NEW review follows start, then emit_calls and answers (each entry { callId, answer } or { callId, failure }) until done. The old claims / verdicts, findings and judgements loops are described only as continuing a state saved before the change. This is the only copy outside src/mcp/server.ts and the step handlers that names the old frames (checked by grep across src/, vscode-plugin/src and jetbrains-plugin/src).

postconditions: insrc_guide({ workflow: 'review' }) and insrc_guide({ workflow: 'code-review' }) return the emit_calls / answers loop.

dataModelChanges.details: Optional { jobs, limitChars, lastFrameCallIds }. Absent marks a pre-change state, resumed on today's phases.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: EmitCallsFrame, AnswersInput and CallFailure, the answers phase in both tools, frame packing, and pre-change resume.
Keeps the jobs in step state and drives them with nextCalls, applyAnswer, applyFailure, runStage and result.
Hands the controller enveloped ReviewCalls; answers are matched by callId.
Uses each adapter's controller stage plan (code review offers ux and diagram prompts as today; premise review batches verify).
Frames follow the jobs' chunk plans.
Material comes from the adapters, built from the saved subject and snapshot.
limitChars bounds both each call and each frame.

errorCases.scenario: An answers entry has no callId, an unknown callId, or a callId already used in the same answers turn.
errorCases.detection: handleAnswers checks every entry's callId against the state's lastFrameCallIds, and counts entries per callId.
errorCases.response: The unknown entry is ignored and logged. Every call of the last frame without exactly one valid entry is applied as identifier-mismatch and re-issued once under a new callId.
errorCases.userImpact: No answer is ever taken for another call; the call is offered again.

errorCases.scenario: An answer's inner content fails the call's schema or the stage's validate.
errorCases.detection: applyAnswer validates the envelope's answer against the call schema, then the stage's validate(answer, call).
errorCases.response: invalid-answer: one re-issue with the correction note, then the stage's failure policy.

errorCases.scenario: The controller reports a size refusal.
errorCases.detection: A CallFailure with cause 'size-refusal' (and maxChars when the controller knows it).
errorCases.response: applyFailure re-divides the call's carried atoms and notes within maxChars, or half the refused size, and the new, smaller calls appear in the next frame. The refused prompt is never offered again.

errorCases.scenario: The controller reports a stall or a transient error.
errorCases.response: Re-issued once under a new callId; a second failure applies the stage's policy (fail-review, record-not-judged or record-observation).

errorCases.scenario: A legacy phase (judgements, claims, verdicts, findings) is called on a pipeline state.
errorCases.detection: The phase handler sees state.pipeline present.
errorCases.response: bad-phase error naming 'answers' as the expected phase; the state is kept, so the controller can retry.

errorCases.scenario: phase='answers' on a pre-change state (no pipeline field).
errorCases.response: bad-phase error naming the legacy phase the state expects; the state is kept.

errorCases.scenario: The state token is unknown: swept after an hour idle (sweeps run when a state is saved) or lost in a daemon restart.
errorCases.detection: loadState throws StateTokenNotFound. Both tools' dispatch catches it; insrc_review_step newly maps it to 'state-not-found' instead of 'internal'.
errorCases.response: Today's state-not-found error; the review must be started again.

edgeCases.expected: Today's dimension prompts (ux and diagram included, as today), each an identified call, in one frame when they fit together, otherwise in consecutive frames. The record equals today's for the same answers.

edgeCases.input: A divided code review from the controller.

edgeCases.input: Several small gather calls pending at once (for example obligation calls).
edgeCases.expected: Packed into one frame up to the limit.

migration.stateBefore: A controller review today gets fixed frames (s1 bundle). Code review gets emit_judgements, all dimension prompts in one frame, answered once with judgements (src/daemon/steps/code-review-step/handler.ts:439, src/daemon/steps/code-review-step/handler.ts:496). Premise review gets emit_claims, then emit_verdicts with one batched prompt; template review gets emit_findings (src/daemon/steps/review-step/phases/start.ts:36, src/daemon/steps/review-step/phases/claims.ts:28). No answer carries a call identifier, nothing is divided, and the MCP registry lists only those phases (src/mcp/server.ts:81, src/mcp/server.ts:87).
migration.stateAfter: Every new controller review is driven by emit_calls frames packed up to the limit and an answers phase matched by callId, with per-call failure outcomes. Under the limit, a review gets today's prompts in today's single frame (or today's two frames for a premise review) and gives today's result. Over the limit, the controller walks the daemon's chunks about one call per frame. States saved before the change resume on today's phases.

migrationSteps.action: Add the optional pipeline field to both step state payloads, the shared frame packing and answer matching, and handleAnswers in both tools, with unit tests.

Switch every controller-review entry to build the jobs and return emit_calls: both handleStart paths, and beginDiffOnlyReview for the declined, freshness-timeout and hollow-grounding fallbacks. Keep the legacy phase handlers for states without the pipeline field, and make them return bad-phase on pipeline states. Map StateTokenNotFound to state-not-found in insrc_review_step's dispatch.
Add 'answers' to both tools' input schemas, the registry phase lists and the tool descriptions in src/mcp/server.ts, with schema-registry and schema-handler tests.

Update the review and code-review sections of src/prompts/steering-block.md (served by insrc_guide, and re-stamped into marked repos' CLAUDE.md steering blocks by the boot steering refresh after the daemon update).
Rebuild and update the installed daemon and the MCP server, so controllers re-read the tool schemas (the plugins' existing post-update MCP reload nudge covers this).

migration.backwardCompat: The MCP tools keep their names and existing phases; 'answers' and the answers field are additive. The start, confirm_wait, done and error outputs are unchanged. A controller that still sends today's judgements, claims, verdicts or findings on a NEW review gets a bad-phase error naming 'answers', because new reviews always use emit_calls. States saved before the change keep today's phases until they expire or the daemon restarts. Stored records keep their shape.

alternativesConsidered.name: Strictly one call per frame
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Every new controller review is driven one ReviewCall per emit_calls frame, in a fixed order across all of the review's jobs; the controller answers that one call (answer or failure) per answers turn.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Each step's state gains an optional pipeline field: { jobs: ReviewPipelineJob[] } (one per code-review dimension, or one design-review job) plus the saved subject and snapshot. Each turn the step rebuilds the adapters, runs any deterministic stage with runStage, collects the pending calls of all jobs with nextCalls, and offers exactly the next one. The answers turn takes that call's EnvelopedAnswer or CallFailure and maps it to applyAnswer or applyFailure. Under the limit a code review becomes one frame per dimension prompt instead of today's single emit_judgements frame.
pros: Simplest frame rule: one call per frame.
Every frame is bounded by one call's size.
cons: A review under the limit takes several turns where today it takes one, so 'proceeds as today' (ac3) holds only for prompts and results, not for turn count.
More turns mean more state saves and round trips for small reviews.

constraintScore.notes: Same prompts and result, but one turn per call instead of today's one frame.

alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Correct, but under the limit it multiplies turns compared with today.

alternativesConsidered.name: Frames packed with the pending calls up to the limit
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Each emit_calls frame offers every currently pending call of the review's jobs that fits, packed in a fixed order up to limitChars of rendered calls. The controller answers every call in the frame, each with an answer or a failure outcome.
alternativesConsidered.approach: State as in a1. Each turn the step rebuilds the adapters, runs deterministic stages with runStage, and gathers pending calls from every job with nextCalls in a fixed order (code review: today's dimension order; design review: stage order). It packs them into one frame whose summed rendered size (messages, schema and envelope of each call) stays within limitChars, never splitting a call. Under the limit a code review's dimension calls normally fit one frame, as today's emit_judgements does, and a premise review offers extract, then the single batched verify, as today. Over the limit a chunk call nearly fills the limit, so frames carry one call at a time. The answers phase must cover every call in the frame: an EnvelopedAnswer goes to applyAnswer, and a CallFailure to applyFailure with its cause and maxChars. A call left unanswered, or answered under an unknown or wrong callId, is treated as an identifier mismatch and re-issued under a new callId. When every job is done, the step writes today's record (code review) or report (design review). A state without the pipeline field resumes on today's frames.
pros: A review under the limit keeps today's single-frame turns where today's frame held several prompts (ac3).
Over the limit the controller is handed the daemon's chunks about one at a time (ac1).
One frame shape and one answers phase for every new review (sc7).
Every frame stays within the limit, so the controller's own context is bounded.
cons: Packing adds one rule (fit by summed rendered size) and the obligation to answer every offered call.

constraintScore.notes: Over the limit, each chunk call nearly fills a frame, so the daemon's chunks are handed about one at a time.
A missing, unknown or wrong callId is an identifier mismatch, re-issued under a new id.
Today's prompts in today's single frame, each enveloped; today's result.
Jobs kept in step state; driven by nextCalls, applyAnswer, applyFailure and runStage.
A frame's summed rendered calls stay within limitChars.

alternativesConsidered.name: Today's frames under the limit, new frames only when divided
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: New controller reviews under the limit keep emit_judgements, emit_claims, emit_verdicts and emit_findings; only a divided review switches to emit_calls.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The step chooses the frame by the chunk plan: single uses today's frames and phases unchanged, divided uses emit_calls and answers.
pros: The under-limit path is byte-for-byte today's.
cons: Two frame shapes for new reviews, which the HLD rejects (sc7: one frame shape for every new controller review).
Answers under the limit carry no call identifier, which breaks k4.

constraintScore.notes: Only the divided path identifies answers.
Requires one frame shape for every new controller review.
Jobs only on the divided path.

alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Two frame shapes and unidentified answers under the limit.
